name: Find invoices that are past due and still unpaid
description: The TAIL the deterministic chaser leaves behind. `chase_invoices` fires on days 1, 3 and 7 past due and then stops for good; this finds what is still unpaid after that, which is the gap four real invoices sat in for 13 to 31 days. Filters: an unpaid status, and a due date more than 7 days gone so nothing still inside the chaser's milestones is touched. THE UPPER BOUND IS THE OWNER'S, not mine: `{{input.stop_after_days}}` arrives as a negative offset from `agent_config`, chosen on the install dialog. It was a number written into this file, which meant every business on the platform gave up at the same moment regardless of what they sell. Capped at 25. A FILTER ON `sent_at` USED TO SIT HERE and did two wrong things at once: `payment_invoices.sent_at` is the day the INVOICE was delivered and never changes, so for a row that had one it was permanently true and deduped nothing — and it is NULL on any invoice that never went through `sendInvoice`, which includes real ones an owner raised by hand, so `NULL < date` dropped those rows before this step returned. That is why the agent ran on schedule, reported success, and sent nothing. Dedup is not this step's job: `sendInvoiceChase` holds a seven-day cooldown read off `payment_reminders`, keyed on the CLIENT, which also sees the milestone chaser's own sends.

name: Ask for each one
description: One send per client, not per invoice — and the scatter is still over invoices, deliberately. `sendInvoiceChase` is keyed on the CONTACT: the first invoice belonging to a client sends one statement covering every item of theirs past day 7, and that client's remaining invoices in this run hit the cooldown and skip. So consolidation needs no grouping step and no second query — just the right key. Before this, a client holding three late invoices received THREE emails in the same run, each correctly deduped against its own invoice and none able to see the other two. ONE PERSON'S REFUSAL MUST NOT STOP THE REST. In production a failing scatter item re-throws and aborts the whole run unless `continueOnError` is set, and per-person refusals are ordinary here: somebody unsubscribed since the last run, an address that bounces, a transport error. Worst of all, the find is ordered OLDEST FIRST, so the one person who cannot be written to would sit at the top of the list and block everybody behind them on every run, for good. The gather phase already separates the failures from the sends, so the run reports honestly instead of stopping. A skipped item is a no-op rather than a failure, which is what lets '1 sent, 2 already covered' read as a healthy run.

steps.name: Send this client everything they are behind on
steps.description: `remind_invoices` is the CHASE, and the distinction is the whole reason this action exists. `send_invoices` is InvoiceDeliveryService: the invoice document with its PDF, the first time it reaches the client. This plan was built on that by mistake, so a weekly run would have re-sent the same bill to the same people with nothing explaining why. It sends one message per CLIENT. Where that client has a single item past day 7 it is `generateChaseInvoiceEmail` — the exact message the scheduled reminder already sends, so a client cannot tell which route reached them. Where they have several it is `generateOutstandingStatementEmail`: every item once, each invoice number linking to its own payment page, subtotalled per currency and never summed across currencies. It re-reads at send time and refuses anything settled: between the find above and this send a client may simply have paid, and chasing somebody for money they have already sent is the worst thing this plan could do.
